+defmodule Histlog.CLI.Commands.Export do
+  @moduledoc false
+
+  alias Histlog.CLI.Options
+
+  @switches Options.common_switches() ++
+              [
+                format: :string,
+                help: :boolean
+              ]
+
+  @aliases Options.common_aliases() ++ [h: :help]
+
+  def run(argv) do
+    with {:ok, opts, args} <- Options.parse(argv, @switches, @aliases) do
+      if Keyword.get(opts, :help, false) do
+        IO.write(help())
+        :ok
+      else
+        export(opts, args)
+      end
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp export(opts, []) do
+    with {:ok, opts} <- Options.normalize(opts),
+         :ok <- validate_format(Keyword.get(opts, :format, "ndjson")),
+         {:ok, rows} <- Histlog.Query.executions(Keyword.take(opts, [:root, :date])) do
+      Enum.each(rows, &IO.write(JSON.encode!(&1) <> "\n"))
+      :ok
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp export(_opts, args), do: {:error, "unexpected export arguments #{inspect(args)}"}
+
+  defp validate_format("ndjson"), do: :ok
+  defp validate_format(format), do: {:error, "unsupported export format #{inspect(format)}"}
+
+  defp help do
+    """
+    Usage: histlog export [--format ndjson] [--root PATH] [--date YYYY-MM-DD]
+
+    Export derived execution rows as NDJSON for pipelines and migrations.
+    NDJSON is intentionally available through export, not query.
+    """
+  end
+end

+= Consolidate And Verify
+:page-layout: default
+
+`consolidate` reads closed sessions for the selected day, writes daily materialized files, and emits the manifest as JSON.
+
+[source,sh]
+----
+histlog consolidate --root /tmp/histlog --date 2026-05-06
+histlog consolidate --root /tmp/histlog --date 2026-05-06 --rebuild
+----
+
+`consolidate --rebuild` ignores the existing checkpoint for that date and rewrites daily materializations from current closed sessions.
+
+Materialization commit is transaction-like:
+
+* stage daily and execution outputs
+* write a pending transaction record
+* atomically move each staged output into place
+* write the manifest
+* remove the pending record
+
+If a previous run stopped partway through, the next consolidation recovers the pending transaction before scanning new sessions.
+
+`verify` recomputes daily materialization record counts and checksums, then compares them to the manifest.
+
+[source,sh]
+----
+histlog verify --root /tmp/histlog --date 2026-05-06
+----

+= Import History
+:page-layout: default
+
+`import` parses zsh, bash, fish, or native histlog history and stores synthetic import events under `imports/`.
+
+[source,sh]
+----
+histlog import test/fixtures/import/zsh_history \
+  --root /tmp/histlog \
+  --date 2026-05-06 \
+  --source zsh_history
+----
+
+Supported sources:
+
+* `zsh_history`
+* `bash_history`
+* `fish_history`
+* `native`
+
+Imported records become synthetic event streams.
+They do not mutate canonical session logs.

+= Install And Build
+:page-layout: default
+
+The Elixir app exposes an escript entrypoint.
+
+[source,sh]
+----
+cd app
+mix escript.build
+./histlog query --help
+----
+
+From the repository root, `make build` compiles the application and rebuilds `app/histlog`.
+
+[source,sh]
+----
+make build
+make install
+----
+
+`make install` symlinks `${PREFIX:-$HOME/.local}/bin/histlog` to the repo-built `app/histlog`.
+That local-development install keeps interactive shells on the latest rebuilt escript without a daemon.
+
+Quality gates:
+
+[source,sh]
+----
+make format
+make format-check
+make lint
+make test
+make ci
+----

+= Paths And Sessions
+:page-layout: default
+
+`paths` summarizes filesystem locations observed as working directories and path-like command arguments.
+Argument paths are recognized by expanding command arguments that point to valid local filesystem paths.
+
+[source,sh]
+----
+histlog paths --root /tmp/histlog --date 2026-05-06
+histlog paths --plain
+histlog paths --json
+----
+
+`sessions` lists recorded shell sessions and can include additional metadata.
+
+[source,sh]
+----
+histlog sessions --root /tmp/histlog --date 2026-05-06
+histlog sessions --details
+histlog sessions --json
+----

@@ -0,0 +1,25 @@
+= Query History
+:page-layout: default
+
+`query` searches derived execution rows from daily materializations, imports, and currently live sessions.
+It prints a colorized human-readable table by default.
+
+[source,sh]
+----
+histlog query --root /tmp/histlog --date 2026-05-06 --command mix
+histlog query --root /tmp/histlog --date 2026-05-06 --command mix --json
+histlog query --today --failed
+histlog query "mix test" --plain
+----
+
+Public output modes are:
+
+* `--json`
+* `--yaml`
+* `--plain`
+* `--format bash|zsh|fish|nu|powershell`
+
+NDJSON remains an internal storage format and is not a query output mode.
+Use `histlog export --format ndjson` for pipelines that need line-oriented JSON.
+
+Malformed query filters, such as invalid regular expressions or duration expressions, return an error instead of an empty result set.

+= Shell Integration
+:page-layout: default
+
+histlog does not edit shell rc files.
+Print the integration code and opt in explicitly:
+
+[source,sh]
+----
+eval "$(histlog init zsh)"
+eval "$(histlog init bash)"
+histlog init fish | source
+----
+
+Pass the shell explicitly when writing setup files.
+`histlog init` auto-detects the shell from `HISTLOG_SHELL`, then `SHELL`, and then reports an error when detection fails.
+
+Pin an exact executable with an absolute path:
+
+[source,sh]
+----
+eval "$(histlog init zsh --binary /absolute/path/to/histlog)"
+----
+
+When `--binary` is supplied, the generated script assigns `HISTLOG_BIN` directly instead of honoring a pre-existing environment value.
+
+Durability modes are `safe`, `balanced`, and `fast`; `balanced` is the default.
+
+[source,sh]
+----
+eval "$(histlog init zsh --durability balanced)"
+----
+
+The generated shell code is a thin capture adapter.
+It calls the internal hook boundary and does not construct history records itself.
+
+Bash integration uses the shell `DEBUG` trap.
+In v1 it installs histlog's trap directly and does not compose with an existing `DEBUG` trap; users with complex bash instrumentation should prefer zsh or fish integration, or review their trap setup before enabling histlog.

+---
+id: 20260507011500
+aliases: ["blueprint intake gate", "histlog2 intake gate"]
+tags: ["cli", "product", "architecture"]
+---
+histlog2 behavior enters histlog v1 only through an explicit intake gate.
+
+## What
+
+The Elixir rewrite may adopt mature `histlog2` workflows when they improve the user-facing tool, but each imported behavior must fit the v1 file-backed architecture.
+
+## Why
+
+`histlog2` is a useful functional blueprint, but it also carries database-era assumptions. Without a gate, the rewrite can copy broad CLI complexity faster than the append-only storage and query model can support it cleanly.
+
+## Gate
+
+A behavior may enter v1 only when it can be implemented over one of these sources:
+
+- daily execution rows
+- currently live session rows
+- import event streams
+
+The behavior must not mutate canonical session events. If it requires in-place history changes, resident indexing, SQL semantics, or a daemon, defer it outside v1.
+
+## Links
+
+- [[Histlog2 Functional Blueprint]] - Describes the source of reusable product behavior.
+- [[NDJSON Boundary Contract]] - Defines file-backed subsystem boundaries.
+- [[No Long Running Service]] - Keeps runtime work short-lived.
